Tessa — replying with technical facts and constraints (inline answers).

- Region guarantee: Yes — for Dedicated and Private deployments we can restrict the data plane to a single AZ/region (eu-west-1) and ensure all inference requests, token logs, and KV cache replicas remain in that region. For Hosted customers we offer region pinning to eu-west-1 with the caveat that control-plane metadata is by default in our control plane region (see below). Model artifacts (weights) can be provisioned in eu-west-1 and are not replicated outside the region unless configured for multi-region failover.

- Private connectivity model: Supported options: AWS PrivateLink (recommended) or dedicated VPC peering via transit. PrivateLink: we provide a managed endpoint service in eu-west-1; customer creates an interface endpoint in their VPC. Allowed: customer-owned private IP ranges on the endpoint ENIs; route table control remains with the customer. Typical lead time: 2–4 weeks for standard customers (certificate exchange + network security review); 4–6 weeks if we need custom IP allocations or manual approvals. No inbound ports required beyond HTTPS to the endpoint; no SNAT for data plane traffic when using PrivateLink. Diagram attached (privatelink-design-v1.pdf).

- Key management: We support CMEK via AWS KMS for data at rest and for encrypting cache artifacts. Pattern: customer creates an AWS KMS key, grants cross-account decrypt/encrypt via a grant we consume from our service account in eu-west-1. HSM: we integrate with partner HSMs for higher-assurance key handling (this is an add-on and requires configuration). Key rotation is customer controlled; we have tooling to rotate access grants without taking services offline.

- Control plane: Our control plane (metadata, orchestration, telemetry) is by default hosted in us-east-1. It contains ephemeral request metadata (request_id, model_version, request size), routing decisions, and billing metrics. We do NOT persist raw prompts in the control plane; raw prompt/artifacts are kept in the region-bound data plane for Private deployments. For customers with stricter needs we offer a Private control plane option (part of Redwood Private) that can be deployed into the customer's VPC or VPC-connected subnet to eliminate cross-region control-plane footprints.

- Audit logs & retention: Default token/log retention is 90 days in our standard plan; logs can be exported to customer S3 (cross-account replication or role-based push) for longer-term retention (30/90/365+ days). We can provide an S3 export + Glue cataloging pattern as part of onboarding. Audit logs include request IDs, timestamps, latencies, and anonymized token metrics.

Other operational notes:
- Fallback behavior: In the event of eu-west-1 capacity exhaustion we can either queue requests, failover to an in-region model variant, or (only with explicit customer opt-in) relay to a non-EU fallback region. We will not move data plane processing outside of the region without explicit, documented customer authorization.
- Data exfiltration controls: egress is via the PrivateLink endpoint; we support VPC endpoint policies to restrict allowed services/hosts and additional firewall rules at the customer's edge.

Attaching the network diagram and a brief connectivity checklist. Lead times above assume an active SOW for Dedicated/Private onboarding; for Hosted pinning there are additional controls but slightly longer lead time for certificate & entitlement checks.

-Markus

Adding the ops/controls perspective and a draft statement.

Operational constraints to call out in the custody statement:
- Maintenance windows: we schedule non-disruptive infra updates in eu-west-1 weekly during a window we will coordinate; critical patches may require short restarts which we announce 72 hours in advance.
- SLA & exceptions: Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime; Private customers get additional scheduling controls. Any manual failover that crosses regions will require written approval and a change control ticket.
- Data retention options: Default 90 days; extended archival available via S3 export (customer pays storage).
- Onboarding timeline:
  * Week 0–1: legal & SOC/SIG packet exchange + Network information worksheet (CIDR, allowed ENIs)
  * Week 2–4: PrivateLink provisioning, cert exchange, endpoint validation
  * Week 4–6: KMS cross-account grants + e2e test run
  * Week 6+: pilot, SLA enablement (if Dedicated)

I attached a short draft custody statement you can send to Marcus. It summarizes commitments and references our SOC 2 and SIG contact. Please review and let me know if any line requires legal language.

-Naomi

Hi Marcus / Sophie —

Thanks again — please find our concise custody & connectivity commitments below and attached a formal draft statement for procurement/legal. If this aligns with what you need we can: 1) kick off the network worksheet, and 2) schedule the PrivateLink provisioning slot.

Summary commitments (short):
- Data residency: For the ClientCorp tenant we will provision the data plane in eu-west-1 only. All inference request bodies, token logs, and cache replicas will remain in eu-west-1 and not be replicated outside the region unless ClientCorp explicitly authorizes failover in writing.
- Private connectivity: We will use AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint) in eu-west-1. Customer retains control of endpoint ENIs, route tables, and private IP ranges. Typical provisioning lead time: 2–4 weeks (standard).
- Key management: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (CMEK); cross-account grants are used to enable encryption operations from the Redwood service account. HSM-backed keys available as an add-on.
- Control plane: Default control plane metadata is hosted in our control plane region; it does NOT contain raw prompts. If desired, we can deploy a Private control plane (part of Redwood Private) to eliminate control-plane cross-region metadata.
- Audit & retention: Default retention is 90 days; audit logs and token metrics can be exported to your S3 (cross-account) for long-term storage.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Marcus: confirm the CIDR(s) for the endpoint & preferred maintenance windows (reply to this thread).
2) If agreed, sign the attached custody statement and we’ll generate the network worksheet. I can also kick off a DocuSign for the SOW addendum if you prefer — provisional HubSpot record: CL-4987.
